content.text: Read all of this leaflet carefully before your child starts taking this medicine because it contains important information.

content.Name: $ID/[No character style]

content.Name: $ID/[No character style]

content.Name: $ID/[No character style]

content.Name: $ID/[No character style]

content.Name: bold
content.text: 1.	What Spexotras is and what it is used for

content.Name: $ID/[No character style]
content.text: Spexotras is a medicine that contains the active substance trametinib.

content.Name: $ID/[No character style]
content.text: It is used in combination with another medicine (dabrafenib dispersible tablets) in children aged 1 year and older to treat a type of brain tumour called glioma.

content.Name: $ID/[No character style]
content.text: Spexotras can be used in patients with:

content.Name: $ID/[No character style]
content.text: •	high-grade glioma when the patient has received at least one radiation and/or chemotherapy treatment.

content.Name: $ID/[No character style]
content.text: Spexotras in combination with dabrafenib dispersible tablets is used to treat patients whose brain tumour has a specific mutation (change) in the so-called BRAF gene. This mutation causes the body to make faulty proteins which in turn may cause the tumour to develop. The doctor will test for this mutation before starting treatment.

content.Name: $ID/[No character style]
content.text: In combination with dabrafenib, Spexotras targets these faulty proteins and slows down or stops the development of the tumour.

content.Name: bold
content.text: Also read the leaflet for dabrafenib dispersible tablets.

content.Name: bold
content.text: 2.	What you need to know before you give Spexotras

content.Name: $ID/[No character style]
content.text: to trametinib or any of the other ingredients of this medicine (listed in section 6).

content.Name: $ID/[No character style]
content.text: Talk to the doctor before giving Spexotras. The doctor needs to know if your child:

content.Name: $ID/[No character style]
content.text: such as heart failure or problems with the way their heart beats.

content.Name: $ID/[No character style]
content.text: , including difficulty in breathing often accompanied by a dry cough, shortness of breath and fatigue.

content.Name: $ID/[No character style]
content.text: including blockage of the vein draining the eye (retinal vein occlusion) or swelling in the eye which may be caused by fluid leakage (chorioretinopathy).

content.Name: $ID/[No character style]
content.text: such as diverticulitis (inflamed pouches in the colon) or metastases to the gastrointestinal tract.

content.Name: $ID/[No character style]
content.text: re your child starts taking Spexotras, during and after their treatment, the doctor will make checks to avoid complications.

content.Name: $ID/[No character style]
content.text: The treatment may cause skin cancer. Usually, these skin changes remain local and can be removed with surgery and the treatment can be continued without interruption The doctor may check your child’s skin before and regularly during treatment.

content.Name: $ID/[No character style]
content.text: Check your child’s skin monthly during the treatment and for 6 months after they stop taking this medicine.

content.Name: $ID/[No character style]
content.text: as soon as possible if you notice any changes to your child’s

content.Name: $ID/[No character style]
content.text: skin such as a new wart, skin sore or reddish bump that bleeds or does not heal, or a change in the size or colour of a mole.

content.Name: $ID/[No character style]
content.text: If your child experiences the following symptoms,

content.Name: $ID/[No character style]
content.text: immediately as this can be a life-threatening condition: nausea, shortness of breath, irregular heartbeat, muscular cramps, seizures, clouding of urine, decrease in urine output and tiredness. These may be caused by a group of metabolic complications that can occur during treatment of cancer that are caused by the breakdown products of dying cancer cells (tumour lysis syndrome or TLS) and can lead to changes in kidney function (see also section 4).

content.Name: $ID/[No character style]
content.text: Spexotras in combination with dabrafenib dispersible tablets has not been tested in children younger than 1 year old. Therefore, Spexotras is not recommended in this age group.

content.Name: bold
content.text: Patients older than 18 years of age

content.Name: $ID/[No character style]
content.text: Information on treating patients older than 18 years of age with glioma is limited, therefore continued treatment into adulthood should be assessed by the doctor.

content.Name: $ID/[No character style]
content.text: Before starting treatment, tell the doctor, pharmacist or nurse if your child is taking, has recently taken or might take any other medicines, including medicines used to thin the blood or any other medicines obtained without a prescription.

content.Name: $ID/[No character style]
content.text: •	If your child is pregnant, or if you think your child may be pregnant, ask the doctor or nurse for advice before taking this medicine. Spexotras can harm the unborn baby.

content.Name: $ID/[No character style]
content.text: •	If your child becomes pregnant while taking this medicine, tell the doctor immediately.

content.Name: $ID/[No character style]
content.text: It is not known whether Spexotras can pass into breast milk. If your child is breast-feeding, or planning to breast-feed, you must tell the doctor. You, your child and the doctor will decide if they will take Spexotras or breast-feed.

content.Name: $ID/[No character style]
content.text: Spexotras may impair fertility in both males and females.

content.Name: italic
content.text: Taking Spexotras with dabrafenib dispersible tablets:

content.Name: $ID/[No character style]
content.text: Dabrafenib may reduce sperm count and this may not return to normal levels after stopping treatment with dabrafenib.

content.Name: $ID/[No character style]
content.text: Prior to starting treatment with dabrafenib dispersible tablets, talk to the doctor about options to improve your child’s chances to have children in the future.

content.Name: $ID/[No character style]
content.text: •	If your child could become pregnant, they must use a reliable method of birth control (contraception) while they are taking Spexotras and for at least 16 weeks after they stop taking it.

content.Name: $ID/[No character style]
content.text: •	Birth control containing hormones (such as pills, injections or patches) may not work as well while taking Spexotras in combination with dabrafenib dispersible tablets. An alternative effective method of birth control should be used to avoid the risk of pregnancy while taking this combination of medicines. Ask the doctor or nurse for advice.

content.Name: $ID/[No character style]
content.text: Spexotras can have side effects that may affect your child’s ability to drive, ride a bike/scooter, use machines, or take part in other activities that need alertness. If your child has problems with vision or feels tired or weak, or their energy levels are low, they should avoid such activities.

content.Name: $ID/[No character style]
content.text: Descriptions of these effects can be found in section 4. Read all the information in this leaflet for guidance.

content.Name: $ID/[No character style]
content.text: Discuss with the doctor, pharmacist or nurse if you are unsure about anything. Your child’s disease, symptoms and treatment situation may also affect their ability to take part in such activities.

content.Name: $ID/[No character style]
content.text: This medicine contains 100 mg of a cyclodextrin in each ml Spexotras of oral solution.

content.Name: $ID/[No character style]
content.text: This medicine contains 1.98 mg sodium (main component of cooking/table salt) in each ml of Spexotras oral solution. This is equivalent to 4% of the recommended maximum daily dietary intake of sodium for an adult at the highest recommended trametinib dose.

content.Name: $ID/[No character style]
content.text: This medicine contains potassium, less than 1 mmol (39 mg) per maximum daily dose, i.e. essentially ‘potassium-free’.

content.Name: $ID/[No character style]
content.text: Always give this medicine to your child exactly as the doctor, pharmacist or nurse has told you. Check with the doctor, pharmacist or nurse if you are not sure.

content.Name: $ID/[No character style]
content.text: The doctor will decide on the correct dose of Spexotras based on your child’s body weight.

content.Name: $ID/[No character style]
content.text: t your child should be given a lower dose if they get side effects.

content.Name: $ID/[No character style]
content.text: Please read the Instructions for Use at the end of this leaflet for details on how to give the oral solution. The oral solution will be prepared for you by your pharmacist.

content.Name: $ID/[No character style]
content.text: . Giving Spexotras at the same time each day will help you to remember when to give the medicine. Give Spexotras with

content.Name: $ID/[No character style]
content.text: the evening dose of dabrafenib dispersible tablets. The dabrafenib doses should be given about 12 hours apart.

content.Name: $ID/[No character style]
content.text: •	Give Spexotras on an empty stomach, at least one hour before or two hours after a meal, this means that:

content.Name: $ID/[No character style]
content.text: after taking Spexotras, your child must wait

content.Name: $ID/[No character style]
content.text: after eating, your child must wait

content.Name: $ID/[No character style]
content.text: if necessary, breast-feeding and/or baby formula may be given on demand.

content.Name: bold
content.text: If you give more Spexotras than you should

content.Name: $ID/[No character style]
content.text: If you give too much Spexotras,

content.Name: bold
content.text: contact the doctor, pharmacist or nurse for advice

content.Name: $ID/[No character style]
content.text: . If possible, show them the Spexotras pack and this leaflet.

content.Name: bold
content.text: If you forget to give Spexotras

content.Name: $ID/[No character style]
content.text: If the missed dose is less than 12 hours late, give it as soon as you remember.

content.Name: $ID/[No character style]
content.text: If the missed dose is 12 hours or more than 12 hours late, skip that dose. Give the next dose at the usual time and carry on giving Spexotras at regular times as usual.

content.Name: $ID/[No character style]
content.text: Do not give a double dose to make up for a forgotten dose.

content.Name: bold
content.text: If your child vomits after taking Spexotras

content.Name: $ID/[No character style]
content.text: If your child vomits after taking Spexotras, do not give another dose until the next scheduled dose.

content.Name: $ID/[No character style]
content.text: Give Spexotras for as long as the doctor recommends. Do not stop unless the doctor advises you to.

content.Name: $ID/[No character style]
content.text: If you have any further questions on the use of this medicine, ask the doctor, pharmacist or nurse.

content.Name: $ID/[No character style]
content.text: Like all medicines, this medicine can cause side effects, although not everybody gets them.

content.Name: bold
content.text: Stop giving this medicine and seek urgent medical attention if your child has any of the following symptoms:

content.Name: $ID/[No character style]
content.text: •	coughing up of blood, passing blood in urine, vomit containing blood or that looks like “coffee grounds”, red or black stools that look like tar. These may be signs of bleeding.

content.Name: $ID/[No character style]
content.text: •	chest pain or shortness of breath, sometimes with fever or cough. These may be signs of pneumonitis or inflamed lungs (interstitial lung disease).

content.Name: $ID/[No character style]
content.text: blurred vision, loss of vision or other vision changes. These may be signs of retinal detachment.

content.Name: $ID/[No character style]
content.text: •	eye redness, eye pain, increased sensitivity to light. These may be signs of uveitis.

content.Name: $ID/[No character style]
content.text: •	unexplained muscle pain, muscle cramps or muscle weakness, dark urine. These may be signs of rhabdomyolysis.

content.Name: $ID/[No character style]
content.text: •	strong abdominal pain. This may be a sign of pancreatitis.

content.Name: $ID/[No character style]
content.text: •	fever, swollen lymph glands, bruising or skin rash at the same time. These may be signs of a condition where the immune system makes too many infection-fighting cells that may cause various symptoms (haemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis).

content.Name: $ID/[No character style]
content.text: •	nausea, shortness of breath, irregular heartbeat, muscular cramps, seizures, clouding of urine, decrease in urine output and tiredness. These may be signs of a condition resulting from a rapid breakdown of cancer cells which in some people may be fatal (tumour lysis syndrome or TLS).

content.Name: $ID/[No character style]
content.text: •	reddish patches on the trunk that are circular or target-shaped, with or without central blisters, skin peeling, ulcers of the mouth, throat, nose, genitals and eyes. These may be signs of serious skin rashes, which can be life-threatening, and can be preceded by fever and flu-like symptoms (Stevens-Johnson syndrome), widespread rash, fever and enlarged lymph nodes (DRESS).

content.Name: $ID/[No character style]
content.text: •	Diarrhoea, feeling sick (nausea), being sick (vomiting), constipation, stomach ache

content.Name: $ID/[No character style]
content.text: •	Skin problems such as rash, acne-like rash, dry or itching skin, redness of skin

content.Name: $ID/[No character style]
content.text: •	Pain in arms or legs or joints

content.Name: $ID/[No character style]
content.text: •	Lack of energy or feeling weak or tired

content.Name: $ID/[No character style]
content.text: •	Increase of liver enzymes seen in blood tests

content.Name: $ID/[No character style]
content.text: •	Decreased level of white blood cells (neutropenia, leukopenia)

content.Name: $ID/[No character style]
content.text: •	Decreased level of red blood cells (anaemia)

content.Name: $ID/[No character style]
content.text: •	Upper respiratory tract infections with symptoms such as sore throat and stuffy nose (nasopharyngitis)

content.Name: $ID/[No character style]
content.text: •	Frequent urination with pain or burning sensation (urinary tract infection)

content.Name: $ID/[No character style]
content.text: •	Skin effects including infection of the skin (cellulitis), inflammation of hair follicles in the skin, inflamed flaky skin (dermatitis exfoliative generalised), wart-like growths (skin papilloma), thickening of the outer layer of the skin (hyperkeratosis)

content.Name: $ID/[No character style]
content.text: •	Sore mouth or mouth ulcers, inflammation of mucosa

content.Name: $ID/[No character style]
content.text: •	Inflammation of the fatty layer under the skin (panniculitis)

content.Name: $ID/[No character style]
content.text: •	Unusual loss of hair or thinning

content.Name: $ID/[No character style]
content.text: •	Red, painful hands and feet (hand-foot syndrome)

content.Name: $ID/[No character style]
content.text: •	Tiredness, chest discomfort, light headedness, palpitations (ejection fraction decreased)

content.Name: $ID/[No character style]
content.text: •	Tiredness, chills, sore throat, joint or muscles aching (influenza-like illness)

content.Name: $ID/[No character style]
content.text: •	Abnormal test results related to creatine phosphokinase, an enzyme found mainly in heart, brain and skeletal muscle

content.Name: $ID/[No character style]
content.text: •	Low levels of sodium or phosphate in the blood

content.Name: $ID/[No character style]
content.text: •	Decreased level of blood platelets (cells that help blood to clot)

content.Name: $ID/[No character style]
content.text: on to the side effects described above, the following side effects have so far only been reported in adult patients, but may also occur in children:

content.Name: $ID/[No character style]
content.text: •	problem with the nerves that can produce pain, loss of sensation or tingling in hands and feet and/or muscle weakness (peripheral neuropathy)

content.Name: $ID/[No character style]
content.text: •	increased sensitivity of the skin to sun

content.Name: $ID/[No character style]
content.text: •	inflammatory disease mainly affecting the skin, lung, eyes and lymph nodes (sarcoidosis)

content.Name: $ID/[No character style]
content.text: •	a hole (perforation) in the stomach or intestines

content.Name: $ID/[No character style]
content.text: •	inflammation of the heart muscle which can result in breathlessness, fever, palpitations and chest pain

content.Name: $ID/[No character style]
content.text: hild gets any side effects, talk to the doctor, pharmacist or nurse. This includes any possible side effects not listed in this leaflet. You can also report side effects directly via the Yellow Card Scheme at: www.mhra.gov.uk/yellowcard or search for MHRA Yellow Card in the Google Play or Apple App Store. By reporting side effects you can help provide more information on the safety of this medicine.

content.Name: $ID/[No character style]
content.text: Keep this medicine out of the sight and reach of children.

content.Name: $ID/[No character style]
content.text: Do not use this medicine after the expiry date which is stated on the bottle label and the carton after EXP. The expiry date refers to the last day of that month.

content.Name: $ID/[No character style]
content.text: Store in the original package in order to protect from light and moisture.

content.Name: $ID/[No character style]
content.text: Before reconstitution: Store in a refrigerator (2°

content.Name: $ID/[No character style]
content.text: After reconstitution: Store below 25°C. Do not freeze. Discard any unused solution 35 days after reconstitution.

content.Name: $ID/[No character style]
content.text: Do not throw away any medicines via wastewater or household waste. Ask the pharmacist how to throw away medicines you no longer use. These measures will help protect the environment.

content.Name: bold
content.text: 6.	Contents of the pack and other information

content.Name: $ID/[No character style]
content.text: -	The active substance is trametinib. One bottle contains trametinib dimethyl sulfoxide equivalent to 4.7 mg of trametinib. Each ml of the reconstituted solution contains 0.05 mg of trametinib.

content.Name: $ID/[No character style]
content.text: -	The other ingredients are: sulfobutylbetadex sodium (see section 2

content.Name: $ID/[No character style]
content.text: ), sucralose (E 955), citric acid monohydrate (E 330), disodium phosphate (E 339) (see section 2), potassium sorbate (E 202) (see section 2), methyl parahydroxybenzoate (E 218) (see section 2), and strawberry flavour.

content.Name: bold
content.text: What Spexotras looks like and contents of the pack

content.Name: $ID/[No character style]
content.text: Spexotras 0.05 mg/ml powder for oral solution is a white or almost white powder.

content.Name: $ID/[No character style]
content.text: Spexotras is supplied in an amber glass bottle of 180 ml with a child-resistant screw cap closure, containing 12 g of powder. Each carton contains one bottle, one press-in bottle adapter and one 20 ml re‑usable oral dosing syringe with 0.5 ml graduation marks.

content.text: Ask your healthcare professional or pharmacist to show you how to use Spexotras correctly. Always use Spexotras exactly as your healthcare professional or pharmacist tells you to.

content.Name: bold
content.text: If you have any questions about how to use Spexotras, contact your healthcare professional or pharmacist.
SECTION A ADMINISTRATION VIA ORAL SYRINGE
content.Name: bold

content.text: To administer Spexotras, you will need:
content.Name: $ID/[No character style]

content.text: Bottle adapter (already inserted into the bottle neck)
content.Name: $ID/[No character style]

content.text: In case of spillage or contact of the Spexotras solution with the skin or eyes, follow the information in the “SPILLAGE CLEANING” section.
content.Name: $ID/[No character style]

content.text: Wash and dry your hands before administering Spexotras.
content.Name: $ID/[No character style]

content.text: Check the solution preparation date on the carton.
content.Name: $ID/[No character style]

content.text: administer Spexotras if more than 35 days have passed after solution preparation.
content.Name: $ID/[No character style]

content.text: The printed expiry date on the right side of the bottle label does
content.Name: $ID/[No character style]

content.text: apply to the solution. This printed expiry date applies only to the powder before it is reconstituted into a solution by your pharmacist.
content.Name: $ID/[No character style]

content.text: Gently swirl the bottle for 30 seconds to mix the solution.
content.Name: $ID/[No character style]

content.text: If foam appears, allow the bottle to stand until the foam disappears.
content.Name: $ID/[No character style]

content.text: Remove the child-resistant cap by pushing down on the cap and turning it anti-clockwise.
content.Name: $ID/[No character style]

content.text: Check if there is a bottle adapter already inserted in the bottle neck.
content.Name: $ID/[No character style]

content.text: If not inserted, contact your pharmacist.
content.Name: $ID/[No character style]

content.text: Push the plunger down into the oral syringe as far as it will go to remove all the air inside.
content.Name: $ID/[No character style]

content.text: Place the bottle on a flat surface and hold it upright.
content.Name: $ID/[No character style]

content.text: Insert the tip of the oral syringe into the opening of the bottle adapter.
content.Name: $ID/[No character style]

content.text: Make sure the oral syringe is securely attached.
content.Name: $ID/[No character style]

content.text: Due to air pressure, the plunger may move by itself when you measure your dose during Step 7. Hold the plunger to prevent it moving.
content.Name: $ID/[No character style]

content.text: Carefully turn the bottle upside down and pull the plunger to measure out your dose. With the tip facing up, the
content.Name: $ID/[No character style]

content.text: of the black stopper must line up with your prescribed dose.
content.Name: $ID/[No character style]

content.text: If large air bubbles appear in the syringe, as shown in the pictures, push the medicine back into the bottle and withdraw your dose again. Keep doing this until there are no large air bubbles present. Small air bubbles are acceptable.
content.Name: $ID/[No character style]

content.text: Continue to hold the plunger in place, turn the bottle back around and place it onto a flat surface. Remove the oral syringe from the bottle by gently pulling straight up.
content.Name: $ID/[No character style]

content.text: of the black stopper is at your prescribed dose. If not, repeat Steps 6 to 8.
content.Name: $ID/[No character style]

content.text: If you are administering via oral syringe, continue to Step 10.
content.Name: $ID/[No character style]

content.text: If you are administering via a feeding tube, go to “SECTION B”.
content.Name: $ID/[No character style]

content.text: Place the end of the oral syringe inside the mouth with the tip touching the inside of either cheek.
content.Name: $ID/[No character style]

content.text: Slowly push the plunger all the way down to give the full dose.
content.Name: $ID/[No character style]

content.text: Administering Spexotras to the throat or pushing the plunger too fast may cause choking.
content.Name: $ID/[No character style]

content.text: Check there is no Spexotras left in the oral syringe.
content.Name: $ID/[No character style]

content.text: If there is any solution left in the oral syringe, administer it.
content.Name: $ID/[No character style]

content.text: If your dose is larger than the oral syringe’s capacity, repeat administration until the total volume is delivered.
content.Name: $ID/[No character style]

content.text: Place the cap back on the bottle and turn it clockwise to close it.
content.Name: $ID/[No character style]

content.text: Make sure the cap is securely attached onto the bottle.
content.Name: $ID/[No character style]

content.text: Clean the oral syringe in accordance with the instructions in “SECTION C”, then store the solution and oral syringe in accordance with the instructions in the “STORAGE” section.

content.text: To administer via a feeding tube, read the following information then move to Step 1.
content.Name: $ID/[No character style]

content.text: •	The solution is suitable for administration via a feeding tube.
content.Name: $ID/[No character style]

content.text: •	Use a Nasogastric (NG) or Gastric (G) feeding tube with a
content.Name: $ID/[No character style]

content.Name: $ID/[No character style]

content.text: •	You may need an ENFIT adapter (not included in pack) to connect the 20 ml oral syringe to the feeding tube.
content.Name: $ID/[No character style]

content.text: Flush the feeding tube according to the manufacturer’s instructions immediately before administering Spexotras.
content.Name: $ID/[No character style]

content.text: Follow Steps 1 to 9 in “SECTION A”, then move to Step 3 in this section.
content.Name: $ID/[No character style]

content.text: Connect the 20 ml oral syringe containing Spexotras to the feeding tube. You may need an ENFIT adapter to connect the oral syringe to the feeding tube.
content.Name: $ID/[No character style]

content.text: Apply steady pressure to dispense the solution into the feeding tube.
content.Name: $ID/[No character style]

content.text: Check there is no Spexotras left in the oral syringe. If there is any solution left in the oral syringe, administer it.
content.Name: $ID/[No character style]

content.text: Flush the feeding tube again according to the manufacturer’s instructions.
content.Name: $ID/[No character style]

content.text: To prevent Spexotras coming into contact with other kitchen items, always clean the oral syringe separately from other kitchen items.
content.Name: $ID/[No character style]

content.text: 1.	Fill a glass with warm, soapy water.
content.Name: $ID/[No character style]

content.text: 2.	Place the oral syringe into the glass with the warm, soapy water.
content.Name: $ID/[No character style]

content.text: 3.	Pull water into the oral syringe and empty again 4 to 5 times.
content.Name: $ID/[No character style]

content.text: 4.	Separate the plunger from the barrel.
content.Name: $ID/[No character style]

content.text: 5.	Rinse the glass, plunger and barrel under warm tap water.
content.Name: $ID/[No character style]

content.text: 6.	Leave the plunger and barrel on a dry surface to air dry before next use.
content.Name: $ID/[No character style]

content.text: If Spexotras gets on your skin, wash the area well with soap and water. If Spexotras gets in your eyes, rinse your eyes with water.
content.Name: $ID/[No character style]

content.text: Follow these steps if you spill any Spexotras solution:
content.Name: $ID/[No character style]

content.text: 2.	Soak up the solution completely using an absorbent material, such as paper towels.
content.Name: $ID/[No character style]

content.text: 3.	Place the absorbent material into a sealable plastic bag.
content.Name: $ID/[No character style]

content.text: 4.	Wipe all surfaces exposed to the solution with an alcohol wipe.
content.Name: $ID/[No character style]

content.text: 5.	Place the gloves and wipes into the same plastic bag and seal.
content.Name: $ID/[No character style]

content.text: 6.	Ask the pharmacist how to throw away the plastic bag.
content.Name: $ID/[No character style]

content.text: 7.	Wash your hands well with soap and water.
content.Name: $ID/[No character style]

content.text: Keep your Spexotras solution and oral syringe out of the sight and reach of children.
content.Name: $ID/[No character style]

content.text: Store the solution upright, in the carton provided with the cap tightly closed.
content.Name: $ID/[No character style]

content.text: Store your oral syringe in the carton provided alongside your Spexotras solution.
content.Name: $ID/[No character style]
